title: ListBox

files.content:
/**
 * The load-more sentinel's shared parts, so `GridList.LoadMore`, `Table.LoadMore` and `Tree.LoadMore` are
 * one recipe in three collections rather than three drifting copies — the same reason `field.ts` and
 * `date.tsx` exist.
 */

/**
 * A quiet centred strip at the foot of a list, where the next page arrives.
 *
 * It is deliberately the least conspicuous thing in the component: a page boundary is a seam in the data,
 * not an event, and a reader scrolling past should see the list continue rather than a control.
 */
export const LOAD_MORE =
  'flex items-center justify-center gap-2 p-4 text-[11px] uppercase tracking-[0.08em] text-fg/45'

/**
 * The spinner, in the sentinel's own colour.
 *
 * `motion-safe`, so a reader who has asked for less motion gets a still one rather than none of it.
 */
export function LoadMoreSpinner() {
  return (
    <span
      data-slot="loader"
      aria-hidden="true"
      className="size-3 border border-fg/30 border-t-fg motion-safe:animate-spin"
    />
  )
}

/**
 * The recipes a list of options shares — `ListBox`, the `Select` and `ComboBox` menus, and the `Menu`.
 *
 * Extracted rather than copied, for the reason `field.ts`, `date.tsx` and `loadMore.tsx` exist: an option
 * that looks one way in a select and another way in a standalone list is one component wearing two
 * designs.
 */

/** The scrolling list itself. `p-0` because padding belongs to the option, so a hovered row reaches the edge. */
export const OPTION_LIST = 'max-h-[264px] overflow-auto p-0'

/**
 * The sheet's `.ds-select-option`: 13px at 75%, with the accent reserved for the choice.
 *
 * **`data-[focus-visible]:outline-none` here is deliberate, and is not the bug `Table` and `GridList`
 * had.** Those declared a ring and then disabled it; this option conveys focus with a **background**
 * instead — the way a menu row does — so there is no ring to disable. Its sibling rule below is what
 * actually paints focus.
 */
export const OPTION = [
  'flex items-center justify-between gap-3',
  'px-3.5 py-[11px] text-[13px] text-fg/75',
  'cursor-pointer select-none',
  'data-[hovered]:bg-fg/7 data-[hovered]:text-fg',
  'data-[focus-visible]:outline-none data-[focus-visible]:bg-fg/7 data-[focus-visible]:text-fg',
  'data-[selected]:text-teal',
  // **Disabled dims and does not recolour**, the house rule every other control follows. This was missing
  // until `ListBox`'s own test asserted the opacity of a disabled option and got 1: an option that cannot
  // be chosen looked exactly like one that can, in this list and in the select, combo box and menu above
  // it, which all share this recipe.
  'data-[disabled]:opacity-30 data-[disabled]:cursor-not-allowed',
].join(' ')

docs:
A list of options where the choice is a value, not a set of rows.

```tsx
<ListBox
  aria-label="Region"
  selectionMode="single"
  defaultSelectedKeys={['fra']}
>
  <ListBox.Item id="fra">Frankfurt</ListBox.Item>
  <ListBox.Item id="iad">Ashburn</ListBox.Item>
</ListBox>
```

| Slot               | React Aria            | Notes                                           |
| ------------------ | --------------------- | ----------------------------------------------- |
| `ListBox`          | `ListBox`             | `selectionMode`, `selectedKeys`, `disabledKeys` |
| `ListBox.Item`     | `ListBoxItem`         | One option. `id` is the key                     |
| `ListBox.Section`  | `ListBoxSection`      | A group of options                              |
| `ListBox.Header`   | `Header`              | A section's heading, and its accessible name    |
| `ListBox.LoadMore` | `ListBoxLoadMoreItem` | The next-page sentinel                          |

## This is not `GridList`

A grid list is a set of **rows** — a dashboard's monitors, a run of results — where each row is a thing
you look at and act on. A list box is a set of **options**, where the list's whole purpose is to produce
one value. They look similar and answer different questions, which is why both exist and why an option
and a row are styled differently: an option takes the accent as **text** when chosen, a row takes it as a
border.

It is also distinct from `Select`, `ComboBox` and `Menu`, which you must open. This one stands on the page
with its own border, and it is what those three build their panels out of.

## It found a bug in four components at once

`ListBox` reuses `OPTION` and `OPTION_LIST` from `optionList.ts`, extracted from `ComboBox` rather than
copied — and its own test, asserting the opacity of a disabled option, got **1**.

`disabledKeys` was dimming nothing: the shared recipe had no `data-[disabled]` rule, so an option that
cannot be chosen looked exactly like one that can — **in this list, in the select, in the combo box and in
the menu**, all four of which share that class list. One line fixed all four.

That is the argument for sharing a recipe rather than copying one, made the other way round: a single
component's test becomes a test of every component that wears it.
